memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Did he not say to me, 'She is my sister,' and didn't she also say, 'He is my brother'? I have done this with a clear conscience and clean hands." Then God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I know you did this with a clear conscience, and so I have kept you from sinning against me. That is why I did not let you touch her." - Gen 20:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abimelech pleads his innocence: "I have done this with a clear conscience and clean hands." He was deceived; he acted in good faith. And God's answer is striking: "Yes, I know you did this with a clear conscience." God saw the truth of Abimelech's heart. He was not fooled by the outward situation but knew the man's genuine intentions.

What a comfort this is. God sees our integrity, even when circumstances make us look guilty. He knows the difference between deliberate sin and honest mistake, between a rebellious heart and a deceived one. Nothing is hidden from Him, including the sincerity of our intentions.

But notice something even more wonderful: "I have kept you from sinning against me." God had actively restrained Abimelech, protecting him from committing the very sin he was drawn toward without knowing it. God was not merely observing; He was intervening, guarding this man from evil.

This is a grace we rarely think about - how often God keeps us from sins we don't even realise we were near. How many disasters has He quietly prevented? How many times has He restrained us, redirected us, protected us, without our ever knowing? "He will not let your foot slip" (Ps 121:3). Thank God today not only for the sins He has forgiven, but for the countless sins He has kept you from committing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you trust that God sees your true intentions, even when others misjudge you?
- Have you thanked God for the sins He has kept you from committing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You see my heart and know my true intentions, even when circumstances make me look guilty. And thank You for the many sins You have quietly kept me from. Guard me still, by Your grace.
Amen.
